title: Frontend Engineer
blurb: What a frontend engineer should know, in the order to learn it: the browser, HTML, CSS, JavaScript, accessibility, TypeScript, React and Next.js, state and data, testing, performance, security, tooling, frontend system design and interview prep.
audience: Developers aiming for a frontend or UI-heavy full-stack role

nodes.title: HTTP, DNS and TLS
nodes.summary: Request and response, methods, status codes, headers and everything between typing a URL and the first byte. The classic opening question in frontend loops.
checklist: Walk through what happens from typing a URL to first paint: DNS, TCP, TLS, request, response, parsing
Explain idempotent vs safe methods and when to use GET, POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE
Group status codes (2xx, 3xx, 4xx, 5xx) and explain 301 vs 302 vs 304, and 401 vs 403
Describe what the TLS handshake establishes and why TLS 1.3 needs one round trip
Compare HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2 multiplexing and HTTP/3 over QUIC, and what head-of-line blocking is
Read a request and response in the DevTools Network panel, including timing phases

links.title: Cloudflare: what happens in a TLS handshake
github: what happens when you type a URL

nodes.title: How the browser renders a page
nodes.summary: Parsing, DOM and CSSOM, style, layout, paint and composite. Explains why layout thrashing and render-blocking resources hurt, and underpins every performance answer.
checklist: Draw the pipeline: HTML parse, DOM, CSSOM, render tree, layout, paint, composite
Explain why CSS blocks rendering and synchronous scripts block parsing, and what defer and async change
Say which property changes trigger layout, which only paint and which only composite
Reproduce and fix layout thrashing caused by interleaved DOM reads and writes
Explain the preload scanner and why it matters for resource discovery

links.title: Chrome: inside look at a modern web browser, part 3
web.dev: avoid large, complex layouts and layout thrashing

nodes.title: Browser architecture in depth
nodes.summary: Processes, threads, the compositor and the pipeline that turns frames into pixels. Useful for senior performance conversations about jank and main-thread work.
checklist: Name the browser, renderer, GPU and network processes and why site isolation exists
Explain what runs on the main thread vs the compositor thread
Explain why transform and opacity animations can stay smooth while the main thread is busy
Describe how input events are routed and why non-passive listeners can delay scrolling
Read a frame in the Performance panel and spot a dropped frame

links.title: Chrome: inside look at a modern web browser
Chrome: inside look at a modern web browser, part 2
Chrome: inside look at a modern web browser, part 4

nodes.title: HTTP caching and the network layer
nodes.summary: Cache-Control, ETags, CDNs, service-worker caches and HTTP/2 and HTTP/3. Getting caching right is the cheapest performance win and a frequent interview probe.
checklist: Explain max-age, no-cache, no-store, private, public, immutable and stale-while-revalidate
Describe conditional requests with ETag/If-None-Match and Last-Modified/If-Modified-Since
Design a caching policy for hashed static assets vs HTML documents vs API responses
Explain what a CDN caches, cache keys, Vary and how purging works
Explain where the memory cache, disk cache, service worker and CDN sit in a request

links.title: web.dev: prevent unnecessary network requests with the HTTP cache
Jake Archibald: caching best practices and max-age gotchas

nodes.title: Git and the command line
nodes.summary: Branching, rebasing, resolving conflicts and reading history. Assumed on day one of any job.
checklist: Explain commits, branches and HEAD as pointers in a graph
Choose between merge and rebase, and say when rebasing is unsafe
Resolve a merge conflict and continue a rebase
Use git log, git blame and git bisect to find when a bug was introduced
Undo safely with git restore, git revert and git reflog

nodes.title: Semantic HTML
nodes.summary: Landmarks, headings, lists, buttons vs links and native elements. Semantic markup gives you accessibility, SEO and keyboard support for free.
checklist: Structure a page with header, nav, main, aside, footer and a logical heading outline
Explain button vs link: actions vs navigation, and the keyboard behaviour each gets for free
Use native dialog, details/summary and the popover attribute instead of div-based widgets
Write meaningful alt text and know when an image should have empty alt
Use responsive images with srcset, sizes and picture, plus width and height to avoid layout shift
Validate markup and explain why div soup hurts screen-reader users

nodes.title: Forms and validation
nodes.summary: Labels, input types, native constraint validation and accessible error messages. Forms are where most real product bugs and accessibility failures live.
checklist: Label every control with label/for or wrapping, and group related ones with fieldset and legend
Pick the right input type, inputmode and autocomplete tokens for mobile keyboards and autofill
Use constraint validation (required, pattern, min, max) and the Constraint Validation API
Show errors linked with aria-describedby and move focus to the first invalid field on submit
Explain why client validation is UX only and the server must validate again
Handle submit with FormData and progressive enhancement so the form works before JS loads

nodes.title: SEO and metadata
nodes.summary: Titles, meta descriptions, Open Graph, canonical URLs and why server rendering matters for crawlers. Expected for content and e-commerce teams.
checklist: Set a unique title, meta description and canonical URL per page
Add Open Graph and Twitter card tags and test a link preview
Explain how Googlebot renders JavaScript and why SSR or SSG still helps
Generate sitemap.xml and robots.txt and know what noindex does
Add structured data (JSON-LD) for a product or article

links.title: Google Search Central: SEO starter guide
Google Search Central: JavaScript SEO basics
Next.js docs: metadata and OG images

nodes.title: The cascade, specificity and the box model
nodes.summary: How rules win, inheritance, box-sizing and stacking contexts. Most 'CSS is broken' bugs are cascade or stacking-context bugs.
checklist: Order the cascade: origin and importance, layers, specificity, then source order
Calculate specificity for a selector and explain why :where() has zero specificity
Explain content-box vs border-box and margin collapsing
Name what creates a stacking context and debug a z-index that does not work
Explain inherited vs non-inherited properties and initial, inherit, unset and revert
Explain block vs inline formatting contexts and what display: flow-root does

links.title: Josh Comeau: what the heck, z-index?
MDN: introduction to the CSS box model

nodes.title: Flexbox and Grid
nodes.summary: One-dimensional vs two-dimensional layout, alignment and intrinsic sizing. You will be asked to build a layout live.
checklist: Explain flex-grow, flex-shrink and flex-basis and why min-width: 0 fixes overflowing flex items
Build a holy-grail layout with grid-template-areas
Use repeat(auto-fit, minmax()) for a responsive card grid without media queries
Align items with justify-content, align-items and place-items in both systems
Explain when to pick Flexbox vs Grid and use subgrid to align nested content

links.title: CSS-Tricks: a complete guide to Flexbox
CSS-Tricks: a complete guide to CSS Grid
Josh Comeau: an interactive guide to Flexbox
Josh Comeau: an interactive guide to CSS Grid

nodes.title: Responsive design
nodes.summary: Fluid units, media queries, container queries and mobile-first layouts. Every product ships to phones first.
checklist: Write mobile-first media queries and pick breakpoints from content, not devices
Use rem, em, %, vw, dvh and clamp() for fluid type and spacing
Explain the viewport meta tag and why 100vh breaks on mobile browsers
Make images and video responsive and avoid layout shift with aspect-ratio
Respect user preferences: prefers-reduced-motion, prefers-color-scheme and zoom to 200%

links.title: Utopia: fluid type and space calculator

nodes.title: Modern CSS: container queries, :has and layers
nodes.summary: The CSS features that shipped across browsers in 2023-2025 and replace a lot of JavaScript and preprocessor code. Interviewers now expect you to know them.
checklist: Write a component that adapts with container-type and @container instead of media queries
Use :has() as a parent selector, for example styling a card that contains an image
Organise styles with @layer and explain how layers beat specificity wars
Use native CSS nesting and custom properties for theming
Use subgrid, logical properties and the newer viewport units (svh, lvh, dvh)
Check support with Baseline and @supports before relying on a feature

nodes.title: CSS architecture and design tokens
nodes.summary: How teams keep CSS maintainable: BEM, CSS Modules, utility-first, CSS-in-JS and design tokens as custom properties. A common senior and design-system question.
checklist: Compare BEM, CSS Modules, utility-first and CSS-in-JS on scoping, bundle cost and SSR
Explain why runtime CSS-in-JS conflicts with Server Components and streaming
Model design tokens (colour, spacing, type) as CSS custom properties with a theme switch
Implement dark mode without a flash of the wrong theme
Set up a reset or base layer and keep component styles from leaking

nodes.title: Tailwind CSS
nodes.summary: Utility-first styling with design tokens. The default in most new React and Next.js codebases.
checklist: Explain the utility-first trade-off: no naming, colocated styles, longer class lists
Configure theme tokens with @theme in Tailwind v4
Use responsive, state and dark variants (md:, hover:, focus-visible:, dark:)
Merge conditional classes safely (clsx plus tailwind-merge) in reusable components
Explain how unused utilities are left out of the production CSS

nodes.title: Transitions and animations
nodes.summary: Which properties animate cheaply (transform, opacity), prefers-reduced-motion and when JS animation is justified.
checklist: Explain why animating transform and opacity is cheaper than top, left, width or height
Choose easing curves and durations and write keyframe animations
Respect prefers-reduced-motion with a reduced or no-motion fallback
Use the View Transitions API for page and state transitions
Decide when a JS library (Web Animations API, Motion) is justified over CSS
Use will-change sparingly and explain the memory cost of extra layers

links.title: web.dev: how to create high-performance CSS animations
Josh Comeau: an interactive guide to CSS transitions

nodes.title: Scope, closures, hoisting and coercion
nodes.summary: Lexical scope, closures, hoisting, the temporal dead zone and type coercion. The core of every JavaScript theory round.
checklist: Explain var vs let vs const, hoisting and the temporal dead zone
Explain lexical scope and the scope chain with a nested function example
Use closures for private state, once(), and a counter factory
Explain the classic var-in-a-loop setTimeout bug and two fixes
Explain == vs ===, the main coercion rules and typeof null
Explain pass-by-value of references and shallow vs deep copy with structuredClone

links.title: You Don't Know JS Yet (free book)

nodes.title: this, prototypes and classes
nodes.summary: How this is bound, how the prototype chain resolves properties, and what class syntax compiles down to. A favourite source of tricky output questions.
checklist: Apply the this rules: default, implicit, explicit (call, apply, bind), new and arrow functions
Write a bind polyfill
Explain __proto__ vs prototype and walk a property lookup up the chain
Implement inheritance with Object.create and with class extends and super
Use private fields (#x), static members, getters and setters
Explain how instanceof works and when it gives a wrong answer

links.title: MDN: inheritance and the prototype chain

nodes.title: The event loop
nodes.summary: Call stack, tasks, microtasks, rendering steps and requestAnimationFrame. Output-ordering puzzles are a staple of frontend screens.
checklist: Explain the call stack, task queue and microtask queue and when each runs
Predict the output of mixed setTimeout, Promise.then, queueMicrotask and async/await code
Explain where rendering and requestAnimationFrame fit in a loop iteration
Explain why a long microtask chain can starve rendering
Explain how await suspends a function and resumes it as a microtask

links.title: Jake Archibald: tasks, microtasks, queues and schedules
Philip Roberts: what the heck is the event loop anyway?

nodes.title: Promises and async/await
nodes.summary: Promise states, chaining, error handling, Promise.all/allSettled/race/any and cancellation with AbortController.
checklist: Explain promise states and how values and errors propagate through a chain
Implement Promise.all, Promise.allSettled and Promise.race from scratch
Handle errors with try/catch around await and avoid unhandled rejections
Run async work in sequence vs in parallel and with a concurrency limit
Cancel fetches with AbortController and add a timeout with AbortSignal.timeout
Implement retry with exponential backoff and jitter

nodes.title: The DOM and events
nodes.summary: Querying and mutating the DOM, bubbling and capturing, delegation and passive listeners. Needed for vanilla-JS machine-coding rounds.
checklist: Explain capture, target and bubble phases and stopPropagation vs preventDefault
Implement event delegation for a list whose items are added dynamically
Use passive listeners, once and AbortSignal to manage listeners
Batch DOM writes with DocumentFragment and avoid forced reflows
Dispatch and listen for CustomEvent
Build a small widget (tabs or todo list) in plain JS without a framework

nodes.title: Modules: ESM, CommonJS and bundling
nodes.summary: How import and export work, why ES modules are static, how they differ from CommonJS and what that means for tree-shaking and dual packages.
checklist: Explain static ESM imports vs dynamic import() and live bindings
Compare ESM and CommonJS: loading, require vs import, __dirname and interop pitfalls
Explain how the package.json exports and type fields decide how a file is loaded
Explain why static imports enable tree-shaking and what sideEffects means
Use top-level await and explain how it affects module evaluation order

nodes.title: Iterators, generators and async iteration
nodes.summary: The iteration protocol behind for...of and spread, generators as pausable functions and async iterators for streams. Shows up in lazy-sequence and pagination questions.
checklist: Implement Symbol.iterator on a custom object and use it with for...of and spread
Write a generator and explain how next(), yield and return work together
Build a lazy infinite sequence and take the first n values
Consume a paginated API with an async generator and for await...of
Read a fetch response body stream chunk by chunk

nodes.title: Memory, garbage collection and the engine
nodes.summary: How the engine allocates and collects memory, the usual frontend leaks and enough about V8 (JIT, hidden classes) to reason about performance claims.
checklist: Explain reachability and mark-and-sweep garbage collection
Name common leaks: forgotten listeners, timers, detached DOM nodes, growing caches, closures
Find a leak with heap snapshots and the allocation timeline in DevTools
Use WeakMap, WeakSet and WeakRef and explain when they help
Explain JIT tiers, hidden classes and inline caches at a high level

links.title: Mathias Bynens: shapes and inline caches

nodes.title: Implement it from scratch
nodes.summary: debounce, throttle, Promise.all, deep clone, an event emitter, curry, memoize. The most common frontend coding questions.
checklist: Implement debounce (with leading and trailing options) and throttle
Implement memoize, including a version with a cache key for multiple arguments
Implement curry and compose
Implement deep clone handling arrays, dates and circular references
Implement an event emitter with on, off, once and emit
Implement Array.prototype.map, filter, reduce and flat

nodes.title: Browser APIs: storage, workers, observers
nodes.summary: localStorage vs IndexedDB, Web Workers, IntersectionObserver and ResizeObserver. Shows up in infinite scroll and offline questions.
checklist: Compare cookies, localStorage, sessionStorage and IndexedDB on size, sync vs async and lifetime
Move CPU-heavy work to a Web Worker and talk to it with postMessage
Implement lazy loading or infinite scroll with IntersectionObserver
React to element size changes with ResizeObserver
Use BroadcastChannel or the storage event to sync state across tabs

nodes.title: Accessibility foundations (WCAG)
nodes.summary: Who relies on accessibility, the WCAG principles and levels, colour contrast and screen readers. Increasingly a pass/fail signal in UI rounds.
checklist: Explain the four WCAG principles (perceivable, operable, understandable, robust) and A vs AA
Check colour contrast: 4.5:1 for body text, 3:1 for large text and UI components
Navigate a page with a screen reader (VoiceOver or NVDA) using headings and landmarks
Make content work at 200% zoom and with text spacing changes
Give video captions and do not convey meaning by colour alone
Explain the legal context (ADA, European Accessibility Act) at a high level

links.title: W3C: How to Meet WCAG 2.2 (quick reference)

nodes.title: Semantics, ARIA and the accessibility tree
nodes.summary: How the browser exposes roles, names and states to assistive tech, and when ARIA helps or hurts. 'No ARIA is better than bad ARIA' is the line interviewers want.
checklist: Inspect the accessibility tree in DevTools and read a node's role, name and state
Explain the first rule of ARIA: use a native element when one exists
Compute an accessible name from content, label, aria-label and aria-labelledby
Use aria-expanded, aria-controls, aria-selected and aria-current correctly
Explain why role alone does not add keyboard behaviour

nodes.title: Keyboard and focus management
nodes.summary: Everything must work without a mouse: tab order, visible focus, focus traps in modals and roving tabindex in composite widgets.
checklist: Keep DOM order equal to visual order and avoid positive tabindex
Style :focus-visible so focus is always visible
Trap focus in a modal, close on Escape and return focus to the trigger
Implement roving tabindex with arrow keys for tabs, menus or a listbox
Use inert to hide background content while a dialog is open
Add a skip link and manage focus after client-side route changes

links.title: WAI-ARIA APG: developing a keyboard interface

nodes.title: Dynamic content and live regions
nodes.summary: SPAs change the page without a reload, so screen-reader users miss updates unless you announce them. Covers live regions, toasts, loading states and route changes.
checklist: Use aria-live polite vs assertive and role=status and role=alert appropriately
Announce async results such as 'saved' or '12 results' without moving focus
Make toasts accessible: enough time, dismissible, not the only place for errors
Announce client-side route changes and set the document title
Expose loading state with aria-busy and avoid announcing every skeleton

nodes.title: Testing accessibility
nodes.summary: Automated tools catch only part of the problems; manual keyboard and screen-reader passes catch the rest. Know both and how to put them in CI.
checklist: Run axe in DevTools or Lighthouse and triage the findings
Add axe checks to component tests and Playwright end-to-end tests
Query by role and name in tests so they double as accessibility checks
Do a manual keyboard-only pass and a screen-reader pass on a key flow
Explain what automated tools cannot judge (alt text quality, focus order sense)

nodes.title: TypeScript fundamentals
nodes.summary: Types vs interfaces, unions, literal types, strict mode and typing functions and React props. Expected in nearly every frontend job posting.
checklist: Explain structural typing and why TypeScript types are erased at runtime
Choose between type aliases and interfaces and explain declaration merging
Use union, intersection and literal types and as const
Explain any vs unknown vs never
Turn on strict mode and explain what strictNullChecks and noImplicitAny catch

nodes.title: Narrowing and discriminated unions
nodes.summary: How TypeScript refines a union through control flow, and how discriminated unions make impossible states unrepresentable. The most useful everyday type skill.
checklist: Narrow with typeof, instanceof, in and equality checks
Model async UI state as a discriminated union (idle, loading, success, error)
Write a type guard (x is T) and an assertion function (asserts x is T)
Add an exhaustiveness check with never in a switch
Use satisfies to check a value without widening its type

links.title: TypeScript 4.9 release notes: the satisfies operator

nodes.title: Generics
nodes.summary: Writing functions, hooks and components that work over many types while keeping the types precise. Interviewers ask you to type a helper like groupBy or a generic list.
checklist: Write a generic function and let TypeScript infer the type argument
Constrain a generic with extends and use keyof and indexed access (T[K])
Type a generic React component such as List<T> or Select<T>
Use default type parameters and const type parameters
Explain when a generic is unnecessary and a union or overload is clearer

nodes.title: Practical TypeScript patterns
nodes.summary: Utility types, typing API responses safely, React prop and event types and branded types. The patterns that show up in real codebases.
checklist: Use Partial, Pick, Omit, Record, ReturnType and Awaited
Type React props, children, events and refs, and forwardRef or ref-as-prop
Treat fetched JSON as unknown and parse it instead of casting
Use branded types to stop mixing up ids such as UserId and OrderId
Type a reducer with a discriminated union of actions

nodes.title: Runtime validation with zod
nodes.summary: Types disappear at runtime, so data from APIs, forms and URLs must be validated. Schema libraries give you validation and the static type from one definition.
checklist: Explain why a type assertion on fetched data is a lie and where to validate
Define a zod schema and infer the TypeScript type with z.infer
Validate form input, URL params and environment variables at the boundary
Show useful error messages from a failed parse
Compare zod, valibot and Standard Schema on bundle size and API

nodes.title: Advanced type-level TypeScript
nodes.summary: Conditional, mapped and template literal types and infer. Handy for library authors; rarely asked outside senior roles.
checklist: Write a conditional type and use infer to extract a type
Explain distributive conditional types over unions
Write a mapped type with key remapping (as) and modifiers
Build a template literal type such as typed event names
Solve a few easy and medium type-challenges

nodes.title: How React renders
nodes.summary: Render vs commit, reconciliation, keys and what triggers a re-render. The mental model behind every React debugging question.
checklist: Explain the trigger, render and commit phases
List what causes a re-render: state change, parent render, context change
Explain why key matters when reordering a list and why index keys break state
Explain how React preserves or resets state by position in the tree
Explain batching of state updates in React 18 and later

nodes.title: Hooks and effects
nodes.summary: useState, useEffect, useRef, custom hooks, the rules of hooks and when you do not need an effect.
checklist: Explain the rules of hooks and why call order matters
Write an effect with correct dependencies and a cleanup function
Spot effects that should be derived state or event handlers instead
Explain stale closures in effects and how to fix them
Use useRef for mutable values and DOM access without re-rendering
Extract a custom hook such as useDebounce or useFetch

links.title: react.dev: you might not need an effect
Dan Abramov: a complete guide to useEffect

nodes.title: State, lifting and context
nodes.summary: Where state should live, derived state, reducers and context without re-render storms.
checklist: Decide where state should live and lift it to the closest common parent
Avoid redundant and duplicated state by deriving values during render
Use useReducer for state with many related transitions
Explain why every context consumer re-renders when the value changes
Split contexts or memoise values to limit re-renders

links.title: react.dev: scaling up with reducer and context

nodes.title: Component patterns
nodes.summary: Composition, compound components, controlled vs uncontrolled, headless components and custom hooks. How senior candidates design reusable UI.
checklist: Prefer composition with children and slots over prop drilling and boolean props
Build a compound component (Tabs, Tabs.List, Tabs.Panel) sharing state through context
Support both controlled and uncontrolled usage in one component
Explain headless components (Radix, React Aria) and why they help accessibility
Use error boundaries and Suspense boundaries as layout decisions

links.title: Kent C. Dodds: compound components with React hooks
react.dev: reusing logic with custom hooks

nodes.title: Reconciliation and Fiber internals
nodes.summary: How React diffs trees, what a fiber is and why rendering can be interrupted. Asked at senior level and at companies that build on React heavily.
checklist: Explain the diffing heuristics: element type and key decide reuse
Explain what a fiber is and the work loop that can pause and resume
Explain lanes and update priorities at a high level
Explain why render must be pure and why Strict Mode double-invokes it

nodes.title: React performance
nodes.summary: memo, useMemo, useCallback, the React Compiler, transitions and list virtualisation. How to find the actual slow component with the Profiler.
checklist: Profile with the React DevTools Profiler and find why a component rendered
Use memo, useMemo and useCallback where they help and explain when they do not
Explain what the React Compiler memoises automatically
Move state down or lift content up to avoid re-rendering expensive trees
Virtualise a long list and lazy-load heavy components

nodes.title: Suspense, transitions and concurrent rendering
nodes.summary: Suspense for loading states, useTransition and useDeferredValue for keeping the UI responsive, and streaming SSR. The core of modern React data flow.
checklist: Explain what Suspense waits for and how fallbacks nest
Mark a non-urgent update with useTransition and show isPending
Use useDeferredValue to keep typing responsive while results lag
Explain streaming SSR and selective hydration
Avoid waterfalls by starting data fetches before the component that suspends

links.title: React 18 working group: new Suspense SSR architecture

nodes.title: React Server Components
nodes.summary: Components that run only on the server, ship no JavaScript and can read data directly. Changes where data fetching and the client boundary live.
checklist: Explain what runs on the server vs the client and what 'use client' marks
Explain what can cross the boundary as props (serialisable values, not functions)
Pass Server Components as children into Client Components
Explain the RSC payload and why it is not HTML
Keep secrets and heavy dependencies on the server with server-only

links.title: Josh Comeau: making sense of React Server Components

nodes.title: React 19: Actions and new hooks
nodes.summary: Actions, useActionState, useOptimistic, use() and form actions. What changed in React 19 and how it simplifies mutations.
checklist: Explain Actions and how form action handles pending state and errors
Use useActionState for a form with validation errors
Use useOptimistic for an instant like or add-to-list
Read a promise or context with use()
Use ref as a prop and the new document metadata support

nodes.title: CSR, SSR, SSG, ISR and streaming
nodes.summary: What each strategy costs in TTFB, LCP and server load, and how to pick per route. A guaranteed system-design follow-up.
checklist: Explain CSR, SSR, SSG, ISR and streaming and their effect on TTFB, FCP and LCP
Pick a strategy per route for a marketing page, a dashboard and a product page
Explain hydration, its cost and what partial hydration or islands change
Explain partial prerendering: a static shell with dynamic holes

nodes.title: The App Router
nodes.summary: Layouts, nested routes, Server Components, loading and error boundaries and Server Actions.
checklist: Build nested layouts and pages with the app directory conventions
Add loading.tsx and error.tsx and explain how they map to Suspense and error boundaries
Read async params and searchParams in Next.js 16
Decide what stays a Server Component and what becomes a Client Component
Navigate with Link and explain prefetching

links.title: Next.js docs: Server and Client Components

nodes.title: Advanced routing
nodes.summary: Dynamic segments, route groups, parallel and intercepting routes and route handlers. Needed for modals, dashboards and APIs inside a Next.js app.
checklist: Use dynamic, catch-all and optional catch-all segments
Organise routes with route groups without changing URLs
Build a modal that is also a shareable page with intercepting and parallel routes
Write a route handler (route.ts) and know when to prefer a Server Action
Call notFound() and redirect() and add not-found.tsx

nodes.title: Data fetching and caching in Next.js
nodes.summary: Fetching on the server, revalidation, cache tags and what is cached where. The most confusing part of Next.js and the most asked.
checklist: Fetch data in a Server Component and run independent requests in parallel
Explain what is cached by default in Next.js 16 and what opts in with 'use cache'
Revalidate by time and on demand with revalidateTag and revalidatePath
Explain the client router cache vs the server data cache
Explain what makes a route dynamic (cookies, headers, searchParams)

nodes.title: Server Actions and mutations
nodes.summary: Server Functions called from forms and buttons, with revalidation after the write. Every action is a public endpoint, so it needs its own auth and validation.
checklist: Write a Server Action with 'use server' and call it from a form
Validate input with zod and return field errors to useActionState
Revalidate or redirect after a mutation
Check auth inside every action, because actions are reachable by POST
Show pending and optimistic UI while the action runs

links.title: Next.js blog: how to think about security in Next.js

nodes.title: Auth and security in Next.js
nodes.summary: Sessions in cookies, protecting routes and actions near the data, and why proxy checks are not enough.
checklist: Store a session in an HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite cookie
Build a data access layer that checks the session next to every query
Explain why a proxy check alone is an optimistic redirect, not authorisation
Avoid leaking server data into Client Component props
Add a Content Security Policy with nonces

nodes.title: proxy.ts and the edge
nodes.summary: Next.js 16 renamed middleware to proxy.ts: code that runs before a request is routed. Good for redirects, rewrites and headers, bad for heavy logic or real authorisation.
checklist: Explain what proxy.ts is and why it replaced middleware.ts in Next.js 16
Write a redirect, a rewrite and a header change with a matcher
Explain why proxy should only do optimistic checks
Compare edge and Node.js runtimes on cold start, APIs and limits

nodes.title: Next.js rendering performance
nodes.summary: Streaming with Suspense, image and font optimisation, partial prerendering and measuring the result.
checklist: Stream slow parts of a page behind Suspense boundaries
Use next/image with sizes and priority for the LCP image
Self-host fonts with next/font to avoid layout shift
Load third-party scripts with next/script strategies
Measure the result with Web Vitals reporting

nodes.title: Deploying and scaling Next.js
nodes.summary: Vercel vs self-hosting, serverless function limits, standalone output and caching behind a CDN. Matters when you own the deploy.
checklist: Explain what changes between deploying on Vercel and self-hosting with Node or Docker
Build with output: 'standalone' for a small container image
Explain serverless function limits: duration, cold starts, no long-lived sockets
Configure environment variables per environment and keep secrets server-only

nodes.title: Kinds of state
nodes.summary: UI state, server cache, form state, URL state and global client state each want a different tool. Sorting state into these buckets is the first step of any architecture answer.
checklist: Classify state as local UI, shared client, server cache, form or URL state
Explain why server data copied into a global store goes stale
Pick the simplest tool per kind: useState, context, a store, a query cache, the URL
Explain derived state and why it should not be stored

links.title: Kent C. Dodds: application state management with React
